entry.title: Central Beurling algebras: Weak amenability of the central Beurling algebras on [FC]$^-$ groups
entry.summary: We study weak amenability of central Beurling algebras $ZL^1(G,ω)$. The investigation is a natural extension of the known work on the commutative Beurling algebra $L^1(G,ω)$. For [FC]$^-$ groups we establish a necessary condition and for [FD]$^-$ groups we give sufficient conditions for the weak amenability of $Z\L1o$. For a compactly generated [FC]$^-$ group with the polynomial weight $ω_α(x) = (1 + |x|)^α$, we prove that $ZL^1(G,ω_α)$ is weakly amenable if and only if $α< 1/2$.
entry.arxiv:comment: To appear in the Michigan Math J

entry.title: Non-weakly amenable Beurling algebras
entry.summary: Weak amenability of a weighted group algebra, or a Beurling algebra, is a long-standing open problem. The commutative case has been extensively investigated and fully characterized. We study the non-commutative case. Given a weight function $ω$ on a locally compact group $G$, we characterize derivations from $L^1(G,ω)$ into its dual in terms of certain functions. Then we show that for a locally compact IN group $G$, if there is a non-zero continuous group homomorphism $\varphi$: $G\to \mathbb{C}$ such that $\varphi(x)/ω(x)ω(x^{-1})$ is bounded on $G$, then $L^1(G,ω)$ is not weakly amenable. Some useful criteria that rule out weak amenability of $L^1(G,ω)$ are established. Using them we show that for many polynomial type weights the weighted Heisenberg group algebra is not weakly amenable, neither is the weighted $\boldsymbol{ax+b}$ group algebra. We further study weighted quotient group algebra $L^1(G/H,\hatω)$, where $\hatω$ is the canonical weight on $G/H$ induced by $ω$. We reveal that the kernel of the canonical homomorphism from $L^1(G,ω)$ to $L^1(G/H,\hatω)$ is complemented. This allows us to obtain some sufficient conditions under which $L^1(G/H,\hatω)$ inherits weak amenability of $L^1(G,ω)$. We study further weak amenability of Beurling algebras of subgroups. In general, weak amenability of a Beurling algebra does not pass to the Beurling algebra of a subgroup. However, in some circumstances this inheritance can happen. We also give an example to show that weak amenability of both $L^1(H,ω|_H)$ and $L^1(G/H,\hatω)$ does not ensure weak amenability of $L^1(G,ω)$.
entry.arxiv:comment: To appear in the Indiana University Mathematics Journal

entry.title: Weak amenability of commutative Beurling algebras
entry.summary: For a locally compact Abelian group $G$ and a continuous weight function $ω$ on $G$ we show that the Beurling algebra $L^1(G, ω)$ is weakly amenable if and only if there is no nontrivial continuous group homomorphism $φ$: $G\to \mathbb{C}$ such that $\sup_{t\in G}\frac{|φ(t)|}{ω(t)ω(t^{-1})} < \infty$. Let $\hatω(t) = \limsup_{s\to \infty}ω(ts)/ω(s)$ ($t\in G$). Then $L^1(G, ω)$ is 2-weakly amenable if there is a constant $m> 0$ such that $\liminf_{n\to \infty}\frac{ω(t^n)\hatω(t^{-n})}{n} \leq m$ for all $t\in G$.
entry.arxiv:comment: To appear in Proc. Amer. Math. Soc

entry.title: Weighted Sobolev estimates of the truncated Beurling operator
entry.summary: Given a bounded planar domain $D$ with $W^{k+1, \infty}$ boundary, $ k\in \mathbb Z^+$, and a weight $μ\in A_p, 1<p<\infty$, we show that the corresponding truncated Beurling transform is a bounded operator sending $W^{k, p}(D, μ)$ into itself. Weighted Sobolev estimates for other Cauchy-type integrals are also obtained.

entry.title: Amenability of Beurling algebras, corrigendum to a result in "Generalised notions of amenability, II"
entry.summary: We fix a gap in the proof of a result in our earlier paper "Generalised notions of amenability, II" (J. Funct. Anal. 254 (2008) 1776-1810), and so provide a new proof to a characterization of amenability for Beurling algebras. The result answers a question raised by M. C. White (Bull. London. Math. Soc. 23 (1991) 375-380).

entry.title: The continuity of Beurling density and Beurling dimension of spectra of a class of self-affine spectral measures
entry.summary: It is well-known that the Beurling dimension of the spectra of certain singularly continuous spectral measures possesses an intermediate property. In this paper, we establish that for a class of self-affine spectral measures $μ$, both the Beurling dimension and Beurling density of their spectra attain full flexibility simultaneously. Specifically, for any $t\in (0,\dim_H^w(\supp(μ))]$ and $s\in [0,\infty)$, there exists a spectrum $Λ:=Λ_{t,s}$ of $μ$ satisfying \[\dim_{Be}(Λ)=t\quad\text{and}\quad D_{t}^+(Λ)=s\] where $\dim_H^w$ denotes the pseudo Hausdorff dimension, $\dim_{Be}$ denotes the Beurling dimension and $D_{t}^+$ denotes the $t$-Beurling density. These results provide new insights into the structure of the spectra for a singularly continuous spectral measure.

entry.title: Lebesgue and Hardy Spaces for Symmetric Norms II: A Vector-Valued Beurling Theorem
entry.summary: Suppose $α$ is a rotationally symmetric norm on $L^{\infty}\left(\mathbb{T}\right) $ and $β$ is a "nice" norm on $L^{\infty}\left(Ω,μ\right) $ where $μ$ is a $σ$-finite measure on $Ω$. We prove a version of Beurling's invariant subspace theorem for the space $L^β\left(μ,H^α\right) .$ Our proof uses the recent version of Beurling's theorem on $H^α\left(\mathbb{T}\right) $ proved by the first author and measurable cross-section techniques. Our result significantly extends a result of H. Rezaei, S. Talebzadeh, and D. Y. Shin.
